title: Strict schemas and plugin scope
summary: Reject unknown fields with additionalProperties: false and register routes inside an encapsulated plugin.

scenario.briefing: A client sent an extra role field in the product body and the store accepted it. The catalog routes also need their own scope so shared hooks do not leak across the server.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.
Review an artifact and identify the concrete risks.

hints: Add additionalProperties: false to both object schemas.
Type the plugin parameter as FastifyInstance instead of any.
Keep the routes inside the catalog plugin and register the plugin once.
Read only request.body.name and request.body.price after validation.

misconceptions.description: Assuming a properties list rejects other keys.
misconceptions.feedback: It only documents known keys. Add additionalProperties: false when unknown input must fail.
misconceptions.testDescription: Body and params schemas reject unknown fields.

misconceptions.description: Expecting a plugin hook to apply to routes outside the plugin.
misconceptions.feedback: Encapsulation keeps the hook inside the child context. Register the hook at the scope that needs it or expose it deliberately.
misconceptions.diagnostic: An encapsulated hook does not apply to routes registered outside the plugin.

misconceptions.description: Shipping a permissive schema and an unwrapped plugin.
misconceptions.feedback: Unknown body fields still pass validation, and the encapsulated hook never protects the root route. Block the change.

sections.title: additionalProperties is the strict switch
sections.body: A JSON schema allows unknown keys by default. Setting additionalProperties: false makes the extra field a validation failure instead of silently storing it.

sections.title: Plugins create a scope
sections.body: Fastify registers a plugin in a child context. Hooks and decorators added inside the plugin stay there unless the plugin explicitly exposes them.

sections.title: Register once, near the entry point
sections.body: A plugin does not run until it is registered. Keep registration at the composition root so the route tree and its scope are visible in one place.

vocabulary.definition: The JSON schema keyword that controls whether unknown object keys are allowed.
The rule that a plugin's hooks and decorators stay inside its own scope.
The entry point where plugins and routes are registered.

artifact.title: catalog.ts
artifact.caption: The body schema is permissive and the authentication hook is trapped inside an unrelated plugin.

findings.label: The body schema has no additionalProperties: false, so extra fields pass validation.
The authentication hook lives in a plugin, so it does not apply to the root route.
request.user is assigned without a module augmentation for the request type.
The schema prevents the handler from returning the request body.

verdicts.label: Block the change until the schema and hook scope are fixed.
Ship it; Fastify applies plugin hooks globally.

steps.explanation: Fastify allows unknown keys unless additionalProperties is false, so role reaches the store. Hooks added inside a plugin are encapsulated and never run for the root POST route. Assigning request.user also needs a type augmentation.
hints: Check the body schema for additionalProperties.
Check where the authentication hook is registered.
Check whether request.user has a type declaration.
Reject the false serialization finding and block on scope and validation.
